facts.text: Commerce was founded in 1797 and incorporated in 1834, making it one of Missouri's oldest river villages.
The town’s name comes from its role as a river‑based trade hub on the Mississippi in the early 19th century.
French settlers first occupied the site in 1788, placing Commerce among Missouri’s earliest European settlements after St. Louis and St. Charles.
During the Civil War, Commerce uniquely kept uninterrupted mail service while guerrilla bands shut down delivery elsewhere in Scott County.
A Methodist congregation dates back to 1825, and the first Baptist church appeared only in 1906, marking a shift in the town’s religious landscape.
The Commerce Historical and Genealogy Society houses its museum in an old church on Missouri Street, open the third full weekend each month.
